api.notes: Upstream is controlled-only (`value` boolean or 'indeterminate' + onChange). `checked` is the default (attribute) and the current state (property); `indeterminate` is the mixed state. The `value` attribute is the submitted value (default `on`).
The native `input` fires on every user toggle and `change` once after it (composed, from the host). Neither fires on property writes. Cancel the `click` to keep the old state.
Object `{type, message}`, or the `status-type` and `status-message` attributes. Always shown detached.

hooks.reason: The ring is drawn on the box wrapper with the shared focus-ring module (`:has(:focus-visible)`), which is the indicator's own shape.

hooks.notes: A form layout that says "required by default" is announced (aria-required) without blocking the form.

keyboard.when: focused, not disabled, read-only or busy

keyboard.action: Moves through the checkbox and the label's info button in reading order

form.notes: Form-associated (ElementInternals): submits `name=value` (`on` by default) only while checked, resets to the `checked` attribute, restores on navigation, joins <fieldset disabled>, works with form= and label for. `required` blocks the submit while unchecked; the error is shown after a change, a blur after an edit or a submit attempt, never on form.checkValidity(). A read-only or disabled checkbox is barred from validation.

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default (D-006): `checked` is a property with the `checked` attribute as its default, and native `input`/`change` events report user toggles, instead of a controlled `value` plus onChange. Cancel the `click` to veto a toggle.

`value: 'indeterminate'` is a separate `indeterminate` attribute/property. A user click clears it and checks the box, as a native checkbox does; the form does not reset it (the native property has no reset either).

`changeAction` runs after each user toggle with the new state and the `input` event; the control is busy meanwhile and returns to its previous state if the promise rejects (upstream's optimistic value reverts the same way).

The browser's own message ("Please check this box") is displayed as the detached status after user interaction, on the same clock as `aria-invalid` and `:state(user-invalid)`, announced once; a failed submit focuses the checkbox.
The label's info button is a focusable button with a name (`label-tooltip` is an addition here; upstream Switch has it). The touch target is at least 24px on coarse pointers.

The checkbox draws the shared `tct-checkbox-indicator` directly. Upstream resolves the visual through the indicator registry (`useIndicator('checkbox')`) so a theme can replace it; rendering an arbitrary registered tag needs `unsafeStatic`, which is only allowed in core/security. See `requests`.

Selection is a bright chip, not an accent (checkbox.md): border, checked fill, glyph and disabled border come from the Tecton checkbox roles through the indicator, all >= 3:1 (D-013 Q-05). The pressed overlay is drawn by the owner over the indicator.

requests.reason: CheckboxInput, RadioListItem and Switch render their visual by tag. To honour `defineIndicators()` replacements, core needs a helper that renders a registry-resolved tag (a `staticHtml` template with `unsafeStatic`, allowed only in core/security), e.g. `renderIndicator(tag, {state, size, disabled}, content)`. Until then the default tags are rendered.

core.checkbox-input.notes: Guides: [mwg:form-associated-custom-elements] value, validity, reset and restore through ElementInternals; [mwg:brand-consistent-forms] native checkbox under a branded indicator; [mwg:validate-input-after-interaction] user-invalid timing; [mwg:required-field-feedback] indicators are text; [mwg:accessible-error-announcement] the status is announced once; [mwg:accessible-web-components] the label, description and status share the control's shadow root.

api.notes: The values of the checked options. Until set (or the user toggles), the options carrying the `checked` attribute.
Native `input` then `change`, composed, from the toggled option's checkbox; the list reads them. Neither fires when `values` is written.
Object `{type, message}`, or the `status-type` and `status-message` attributes. Always shown detached.

hooks.notes: Family-private context: values, disabled, hasDisabledMessage, readonly, loadingValue.

keyboard.action: One tab stop per option: the option's checkbox. The row is not focusable and there is no second stop.

form.notes: Multi-value form control: submits one `name=value` entry for each checked option, resets to the options marked `checked`, restores a FormData, joins <fieldset disabled>. `required` means at least one option is checked. The group is the role element (`group`); a blocked submit focuses the first enabled option's checkbox.

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default (D-006): `values` is a property whose default is the options marked `checked`; upstream's optional `value` array + onChange (collection mode) is the same model with the state owned by the caller. Set `values` from the `change` handler to control it.
The list is form-associated (an addition): one entry per checked option under `name`, a `required` constraint, reset and restore. Upstream's list has no `htmlName`.
An item without a `value` is standalone (a select-all row) instead of throwing inside a list with values; an item with a value is always an option.

The list answers the density and dividers context of its rows itself (`listContext`) instead of rendering a `tct-list`: the options are its light-DOM children, and a provider inside its shadow root is not found by a slotted consumer that connected first. The rows draw their own dividers for the same reason (the inner row is always the last of its root).
Validation is displayed after user interaction: the browser's message becomes the detached status, `aria-invalid` on the group and `:state(user-invalid)` flip together.

core.checkbox-list.notes: Guides: [mwg:form-associated-custom-elements] a multi-value control submits a FormData; [mwg:accessible-web-components] the group role and its label live in one shadow root; [mwg:required-field-feedback].

api.notes: A host aria-label names the checkbox (not the row).
Standalone mode: the default (attribute) and current state (property). `indeterminate` is the mixed state.
The native `input` then `change` from the item's checkbox (composed); the state is the item's `checked`.

hooks.reason: The row's description reaches the checkbox as a hidden copy of its text in the checkbox's own shadow root (`data-row-description`): a consumer slotted into a row cannot rely on a provider that renders after it.

form.notes: Inside a checkbox list the list submits the option's value; a standalone item takes no part in a form.

differences.text: `label`, `description` and `end` are attributes and slots: a rich label or description is `slot="label"` / `slot="description"`. A rich label names the checkbox through `aria-labelledby` (the hidden name is the localised word "Checkbox"); a host `aria-label` replaces it.
Checked state comes from the list's `values` for an item with a `value`; `checked` on such an item is ignored (upstream ignores `isChecked` there too).
A checked option tints its whole row with the accent wash (`--color-accent-muted`) through the row's exported part, without `aria-current` on the row (the checkbox carries the state).
